subject: Prod outage: cache collapse causing 504/429 amplification
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus SRE <sre@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Observability spike — 504/429s across inference endpoints

Rishi,

We started seeing a large increase in 504s and 429s hitting our integrations at ~07:45 PDT. Latency for our longest-running routes jumped from p95 ~120ms to >4s and error rate spiked to ~6% (5xx/429). This is impacting our customer-facing flows.

Attached is a dashboard screenshot and a short tail of gateway logs. The errors look like upstream timeouts; we see a lot of retry loops from our side which might be amplifying things. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side? We have a critical morning roll and need a fix or mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform, Nimbus Health

Attachments: prod-504-dashboard.png, gateway-tail-30mar.txt
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability spike — 504/429s across inference endpoints

Elena — thanks for the quick alert and the screenshots. Monica, Marissa — can you triage?

Initial read: our edge is returning 504s when downstream inference workers experience long queue times; the retry storm you mentioned can indeed amplify queueing. I'm asking infra to pull KV-cache and batching metrics; there's a known edge case where prefix-KV invalidation can cause cache thrash under certain request distributions.

Immediate ask for Nimbus: please stop client-side retries for 10 mins (exponential backoff only with large jitter) and route heavy bulk calls to the dedicated batch endpoint if possible. I'll follow up with a mitigation plan inside 30 mins.

—Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability spike — 504/429s across inference endpoints

Rishi — quick update from infra:
- KV-cache eviction rate jumped ~10x starting 07:42 PDT; heap pressure on the cache workers correlates with increased per-request latency.
- Batching queue length on the g4 nodes exploded after many requests missed prefix cache and fell back to cold KV loads.
- Autoscaler didn't trigger immediately because the metric used (GPU utilization) lagged while queues grew.

Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Set per-route concurrency cap and open a short-circuit to return 429s quickly on the worst-hit routes (to avoid long queue buildup).
2) Reduce KV-cache memory limit to force more consistent evictions (short-term) while we stabilize eviction heuristics.
3) Roll forward a small patch to fix a race in prefix invalidation (we have a candidate branch).

I'm preparing a concise mitigation plan and will push logs/trace links to the drive.

Monica
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability spike — 504/429s across inference endpoints

Looping in Markus because Nimbus is threatening to failover and wants an exec commitment on a timeline.

We validated the candidate fix locally (prefix invalidation race). It prevents simultaneous invalidation + write that currently results in large misses and heavy KV reloads. Plan:
- Hotfix rollout to 10% of traffic in us-west within 20 minutes.
- If p95 latency drops by >30% in the canary, expand to 50% in 30 minutes and full roll in 1 hour.
- If canary shows regression, rollback immediately and apply short-term caps outlined by Monica.

I also recommend enabling a one-hour rate cap on the affected customer routes as a protective action (we can do this per-account).

Marissa
Principal Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability spike — cache collapse causing 504/429 amplification

Thanks all for the rapid triage. Rishi — please keep me posted every 30 minutes until stabilized. Priorities: restore customer experience, avoid cascading rollbacks, and collect enough telemetry for a postmortem.

Action items I want tracked in the incident channel (and a short owner for each):
- Canary rollout (Marissa)
- Short-term per-route caps and rate-limits (Monica)
- Customer communication & rollback policy (Rishi)
- Postmortem plan & RCA owner (Sean)

Elena — we'll share the canary dashboard and a clear ETA for the full fix as we validate. Sorry for the disruption; we'll prioritize this.

Markus
VP, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference
